name: Extragonadal Teratoma

criteria.description: Presence of a well-defined mass with heterogeneous components on imaging (CT/MRI) located outside the gonads
Histopathological confirmation of teratomatous tissue containing derivatives of at least two germ layers
Exclusion of primary gonadal germ cell tumor by clinical and imaging evaluation
Elevated serum tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) or beta-hCG in some cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of teratomatous tissue in a mass located outside the gonads with exclusion of gonadal primary tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and histopathology; tumor markers may aid but are not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mediastinal mass with heterogeneous cystic and solid components
searchTerms: chest mass with mixed cyst and solid parts
mediastinal tumor with varied tissue types
mass with both fluid and solid areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sacrococcygeal mass presenting as a palpable lump in neonates

common.notes: Due to mass effect in mediastinal tumors
Compression of airways or lung tissue
In cases of retroperitoneal or pelvic extragonadal teratomas
May be present in malignant transformation

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to spinal cord compression
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure causing neurological signs
weakness or numbness from spinal tumor

occasional.notes: Due to nerve involvement in pelvic tumors
Indicative of immature or malignant components

rare.notes: Rare autoimmune phenomena associated with tumor
Due to compression by mediastinal mass

searchTerms: hydronephrosis due to urine flow obstruction

laboratory: Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) in some cases
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: CT or MRI showing heterogeneous mass with cystic and solid components outside gonads
Calcifications within the mass on imaging
No evidence of primary gonadal tumor
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; germ cell tumors may show isochromosome 12p in some cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating tissues derived from at least two germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm)

distinguishingFeatures: Primary tumor located within gonads (testes or ovaries)
Mediastinal mass but histology shows thymic epithelial cells
Lack of germ cell tumor markers elevation
Common in children with adrenal or paraspinal origin

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass causing airway or vascular compression
Elevated tumor markers suggestive of malignant transformation
Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord or nerve compression
references: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Testicular Cancer
WHO Classification of Tumors of the Urinary System and Male Genital Organs, 4th Edition
